notes: Failed refine, narrowly (AUROC 0.875 vs 0.90 bar; median fire 0.468; 6/8 fire >= 0.30; 1 near miss >= 0.30: a one-token '.' in a political sentence at 0.303). Multi-sentence passages did what one-liners could not (median 0.47 vs 0.29 earlier). New detail: 5 of 8 fire items peak on ' have' in a science-news opener ('Researchers/Physicists/Scientists/Astronomers have detected...', 0.33-0.52), so the strongest part is the auxiliary after a plural science-agent subject, not generic function words. The weakest fire item (0.039) was a 'quantum computer' news passage with no 'have' opener. Not tested: a 'have'-after-scientists label against non-science 'have'. Loop-back: neighbours L9/N926+, L27/N2326-, L34/N5526+, L4/N9075+, L35/N4916+ failed, L7/N3945+ held; none sharpens this pole, so the label keeps science-news register as the frame and the next refine should test ' have' after science-agent subjects.
label: Weak, diffuse pole: ordinary function words (to, the, for, with, more) inside running multi-sentence science-news or research-explainer prose (astronomy, physics, devices, cell biology); near silent in single short sentences, recipes and instructions, fiction, chat, politics, history, code.

qc.label_under_test: Ordinary mid-sentence words (to, with, for, more, the) inside running science and research explainer prose (physics, devices, astronomy, biology, what causes what); weaker for economics and history, low for fiction, chat, recipes, politics news, code and maths.
